intro: Seville rewards wanderers with compact old-town lanes, hidden plazas, tapas bars and flamenco. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro has one line that runs south-west to south-east and misses the old town. Tickets cost €1.30 for one zone.
Trams run about 2 km from Prado de San Sebastián to Plaza Nueva, past the cathedral. Most visitors walk this stretch instead.
City buses are frequent and cover most of the city. A single fare is €1.40, or €0.35–0.38 with a rechargeable bonobus card.
Taxis are easy to find. Cabify, Uber, Bolt and FreeNow all operate, and Cabify is the local favourite. Check the fare before you ride.
Driving in the old city is tricky. Park in a hotel garage, and never leave anything in the car because break-ins are common.
Walking is the best way to see the sights, since the main points are compact. Sevici bikes and Lime scooters are also available. There is no ferry.

cathedral.name: Seville Cathedral
cathedral.hours: Roughly Mon–Sat 11:00–17:00, Sun afternoons only · check on the day
cathedral.tip: Go early on a weekday to avoid the queue, and see Columbus's tomb inside.

alcazar.name: Alcázar of Seville
alcazar.hours: Roughly daily 09:30–17:00 · check on the day
alcazar.tip: Book a timed ticket online, because day tickets sell out in peak months.

giralda.name: Giralda
giralda.price_text: Included with cathedral ticket, approx. EUR 12–15 (check on the day)
giralda.hours: Same as cathedral · check on the day
giralda.tip: Climb the ramps, not stairs, for the city views. Expect a steady climb.

plaza-espana.name: Plaza de España, Seville
plaza-espana.tip: Rent a rowboat on the canal or walk the tiled alcoves to find your province's tile panel.

torre-oro.name: Torre del Oro
torre-oro.hours: Roughly Tue–Sun 10:00–14:00 · check on the day
torre-oro.tip: Small museum about river history; go up top for a quick view over the Guadalquivir.

guadalquivir.name: Guadalquivir River
guadalquivir.price_text: Free to walk along the banks
guadalquivir.tip: Walk the riverside promenade between the Torre del Oro and the Triana Bridge.

river-cruise.name: Guadalquivir River Cruise
river-cruise.hours: Several departures daily, mostly afternoon and evening · check on the day
river-cruise.tip: Choose a cruise with a commentary in your language; evening trips show the bridges lit up.

isla-magica.name: Isla Mágica
isla-magica.hours: Seasonal, usually afternoons; closed some weekdays off-season · check on the day
isla-magica.tip: Check the opening days before you go, since hours change a lot by season.

pizjuan.name: Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan
pizjuan.price_text: Match tickets vary · stadium tours check on the day
pizjuan.hours: Match days only for games; tours on set days · check on the day
pizjuan.tip: Only go if you like football; buy tickets early and expect a loud crowd.

semana-santa.name: Semana Santa
semana-santa.price_text: Free to watch processions · grandstand seats cost extra
semana-santa.hours: Holy Week processions, usually March or April · check on the day
semana-santa.tip: Book a hotel near the procession route early, because the city fills up fast.

setas.name: Setas de Sevilla
setas.hours: Roughly daily 09:30–midnight · check on the day
setas.tip: Book a timed slot for the rooftop walkway, ideally at sunset.

triana-bridge.name: Triana Bridge
triana-bridge.tip: Cross on foot toward Triana for the best river view of the city.

mercado-triana.name: Mercado de Triana
mercado-triana.price_text: Pay per item, approx. EUR 5–15 per snack
mercado-triana.hours: Roughly Mon–Sat mornings to afternoon · check on the day
mercado-triana.tip: Try tapas at the bars inside; go at lunch, when it is busiest and most lively.

santa-cruz-walk.name: Barrio de Santa Cruz walk
santa-cruz-walk.tip: Get lost in the narrow lanes early, then stop for orange-blossom treats at a plaza.

calle-betis-view.name: Calle Betis sunset viewpoint
calle-betis-view.tip: Grab a drink on the riverside terraces and watch the sunset over the Cathedral.

flamenco-show.name: Flamenco show
flamenco-show.hours: Usually evening performances · check on the day
flamenco-show.tip: Choose a smaller venue in Triana or Santa Cruz, and book ahead.

maria-luisa.name: Parque de María Luisa
maria-luisa.tip: Rent a bike or walk the shaded paths, and pause at the fountains.

stays.why: Walk to the Alcázar, the cathedral and the narrow lanes; very atmospheric, but streets are tight and quiet at night.
Across the river from the old town, with tapas bars and flamenco tablaos; a short walk to the centre.
Near the bullring and the river, a short walk to Santa Cruz and the cathedral; busy and convenient.
Local neighbourhood north of the old town, with lower prices; a longer walk or bus ride to the main sights.

food: Eat tapas in small bars: order a few plates to share, such as jamón, croquetas and pimientos de padrón.
Try the bars in Triana along Calle Betis and across the river for lively, local-style evenings.
Eat late: many locals dine after 21:00, so kitchens may be quieter before then.
Pick a sit-down café or bar for breakfast with toast and coffee, usually cheaper than a full meal (check prices on the day).
Ask for the menu del día at lunch for a set meal at a good price (check on the day).
more_time: Take a day trip to Córdoba by train to see the Mezquita and its historic old town.
Visit Itálica, the Roman ruins just outside Seville, for a quieter half-day.
Spend an afternoon at the Plaza de España and Parque de María Luisa for gardens and riverside walks.
